#2230. Nuovo centro sportivo Napoli, oggi la firma dal notaio di De Laurentiis per l’acquisizione dei terreni

Aurelio De Laurentiis ha definito l’accordo per l’acquisto dei terreni dove sorgerà il nuovo centro sportivo. L’appuntamento sarebbe stato fissato mercoledì 18 novembre alle ore 12 nello studio notarile a Chiaia in via dei Mille di Francesco Coppa. Si tratta di un acquisto preliminare, che riguarderebbe suoli per 13 ettari, anche se in futuro nell’affare potrebbero rientrare almeno altri cinque ettari di terreni. Con le firme sui contratti, il presidente e la societ diventeranno ufficialmente proprietari di quasi 13 ettari in località Pozzo Nuovo a Qualiano. Le trattative sono terminate, entro gennaio 2027 inizieranno anche i lavori per la trasformazione dell’area. Il nuovo training center potrebbe essere operativo entro 12 mesi. Perché ora il Napoli ha fretta di spostarsi nella sua nuova casa: e quindi, verrà data la priorità alla realizzazione di (almeno) tre campi di calcio necessari per gli allenamenti della prima squadra, gli spogliatoi, le palestre, le piscine, le aree dei massaggi e quelle per gli uffici. E di una palazzina per il ristoro. Poi, solo in un secondo momento, si aprirà il cantiere per la foresteria e per la realizzazione di un convitto per i giovani. Lo scrive Il Corriere del Mezzogiorno

#2229. “It is an honour” – Yormark speaks after Milan Sport & Entertainment CEO appointment

Earlier today, AC Milan were introduced to a new name, thanks to the creation of a new company: Milan Sports & Entertainment.

The international break is never really a period of major news, yet Milan broke that spell today. Indeed, RedBird Capital Partners published a statement about a new company formed to oversee all of the Rossoneri’s business.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A centralised company that would allow everything Diavolo to be kept in one place is a major step forward for the club and city. San Donato was mentioned as an important focus for the new company, but the headline will remain the footballing operation.

To help with the project, Gerry Cardinale – who spoke about the decision – has appointed Brett Yormark to be the CEO of the company and reports suggest that he will join in January.

Speaking today, via MilanNews, Yormark admitted it was an honour to be part of the Milan family.

“It is an honour and a privilege to take on this role in a city with Milan’s history and passion for sports. I understand the responsibility that comes with leading an organisation tied to institutions that mean so much to their fans and the communities they serve.

“Throughout my career, I have helped evolve sports organisations, expand their reach, and create new opportunities. I look forward to leveraging this experience to realise RedBird’s vision for MSE.

“I am thrilled to work alongside Gerry, RedBird, and our colleagues in Milan to transform this vision into concrete, lasting results.”

#2227. Cardinale: "Quando sono arrivato quattro anni fa a Milano avevo due obiettivi, oltre che vincere: lo stadio e investire nella pallacanestro"

Alla SBJ Dealmakers, la conferenza promossa da Sports Business Journal che è andata in scena nelle scorse ore a New York e che propone diversi panel, tra i quali anche quello su Nba Europe, hanno partecipato anche il vice-commissioner della Nba Mark Tatum e il Managing Partner di RedBird Capital, Gerry Cardinale. Come riporta La Gazzetta dello Sport, il proprietario del Milan ha punzecchiato l'Eurolega che per ora continua a fare muro e non trova un accordo con l'Nba: “Andremo avanti per la nostra strada con o senza un accordo perché sappiamo che alla fine noi saremo quelli che resteranno in piedi. Onestamente non riesco a capire come si possa operare per 26 anni e non riuscire a produrre un profitto. Adam Silver e Mark Tatum stanno facendo di tutto ma per arrivare a un accordo ma bisogna essere in due a fare compromessi. Sono convinto che alla fine la Nba sarà quella che prevarrà”.

Cardinale ha poi continuato: "Milano in questo momento è il mercato più caldo d’Europa. Quando sono arrivato quattro anni fa avevo due obiettivi, oltre che vincere; uno era quello dello stadio, che finalmente si farà e l’altro quello di investire nella pallacanestro e infatti ho avuto conversazioni con l’Olimpia Milano ben prima dell’avvento di Nba Europe. Dove sarà Nba Europe tra 10 anni? Diciamo che se per la nuova franchigia Nba di Las Vegas si parla di una valutazione di 13-14 miliardi di dollari, io penso che tra 10 anni i club di Nba Europe varranno almeno la metà”.

#2225. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

“I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

“He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

“It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. And from what I know, several English clubs are already ready to make him a player.

“So AC Milan could give him a try, but it will require a big project and a lot of money.”

We shall have to see how January develops and whether he could be sold on the project. However, it certainly doesn’t bode well from these comments.

#2224. Frattesi si allena con la Lazio dopo gli esami: può esserci col Lecce

La risonanza ha evidenziato un affaticamento, senza lesioni. Rovella e Gudmundsson hanno lavorato con il gruppo.

Davide Frattesi è tornato ad allenarsi regolarmente con il gruppo della Lazio dopo il problema ai flessori che lo aveva costretto a lasciare in anticipo il ritiro della Nazionale. Gli esami hanno escluso lesioni muscolari e, salvo imprevisti nelle prossime sedute, il centrocampista sarà a disposizione di Gennaro Gattuso per la gara contro il Lecce.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il classe ’99, ex Inter, aveva lasciato Coverciano nei giorni scorsi per un fastidio accusato durante gli impegni con l’Italia. Aveva così saltato la sfida di Bruxelles contro il Belgio, mentre alla Lazio cresceva la preoccupazione per le sue condizioni.

Gli accertamenti strumentali e la risonanza magnetica effettuati nelle ultime ore hanno evidenziato un affaticamento, senza lesioni muscolari. Nella seduta odierna Frattesi ha lavorato con i compagni, mettendosi a disposizione dello staff tecnico dopo il rientro anticipato dal ritiro azzurro.

Se non arriveranno ricadute o altri imprevisti durante la preparazione, il centrocampista sarà convocabile per l’anticipo della 12ª giornata di Serie A contro il Lecce. La partita è in programma sabato 21 novembre alle 15:00 allo Stadio Olimpico.

Il recupero di Frattesi conta per la Lazio anche alla luce del suo rendimento recente. La mezzala è andata a segno nell’ultimo turno di campionato sul campo del Napoli. I suoi inserimenti e la sua freschezza atletica sono risorse per affrontare la difesa del Lecce alla ripresa del torneo.

La seduta ha dato a Gattuso altre indicazioni in vista della sfida con i salentini. Nicolò Rovella, Danilo Cataldi, Albert Gudmundsson, Tijjani Noslin e Kenneth Taylor hanno lavorato regolarmente in gruppo. Il loro coinvolgimento offre al tecnico più soluzioni a centrocampo e nel reparto offensivo.

In particolare, la presenza di Rovella e Gudmundsson amplia le possibilità di rotazione dell’allenatore in vista dei prossimi impegni ravvicinati. Anche per loro, dunque, l’allenamento con i compagni è un passaggio nella preparazione della gara contro il Lecce.

Mano pesante del Giudice Sportivo nei confronti di Serse Cosmi: l'ex tecnico della Salernitana, esonerato a fine ottobre, è stato squalificato per 3 mesi e ha ricevuto 10.000 euro di multa per aver proferito insulti razzisti nei confronti di Marko Butic, attaccante del Bari, in occasione del match del campionato del girone C disputato il 4 ottobre.

Nello specifico, Cosmi avrebbe apostrofato Butic con la frase "sei uno zingaro". Il Giudice Sportivo, in seguito alle indagini di rito, ha deciso di punire severamente Cosmi, sposando la tesi di Butic.

#2218. Lazio-Lecce si avvicina: possibile rientro per un attaccante salentino

Nella 12ª giornata i biancocelesti ospitano i salentini, che sperano di convocare in extremis l'esterno svizzero.

Dopo la sosta torna la Serie A con la 12ª giornata, e sabato alle 15:00 la Lazio scende in campo per difendere il primato contro un Lecce che resta in dubbio per il recupero di Joël Monteiro.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Questa mattina Monteiro ha lavorato ancora a parte per smaltire la lesione rimediata contro il Genoa. Nonostante ciò, in casa giallorossa filtra un cauto ottimismo per una sua possibile convocazione contro i biancocelesti: domani mister Di Francesco lo osserverà con attenzione nella seduta pomeridiana a Martignano.

Oltre al dubbio legato all'esterno svizzero, il tecnico salentino dovrà fare sicuramente a meno di altre due pedine fondamentali per la sfida contro i biancocelesti: Santiago Pierotti, alle prese con la frattura del malleolo che lo terrà fuori fino al 2027, e Ivan Ilić, fermo per una lesione al retto femorale.

#2217. Roma, Dybala scalda i motori e va a caccia del primo gol: sa già come colpire il Parma

Finalmente Paulo Dybala torna a disposizione. Quello che inizialmente sembrava un leggero problema muscolare si è rivelato più serio del previsto: un affaticamento si è rivelato poi una piccola lesione, che lo ha costretto a rimanere lontano dal campo per oltre un mese. Adesso, però, la Joya è pronta a riprendersi la scena.

Dopo essere tornato ad allenarsi in gruppo la scorsa settimana, negli ultimi giorni Dybala ha iniziato a svolgere regolarmente le sedute complete insieme ai compagni. A Parma sarà dunque regolarmente a disposizione di Gasperini e potrebbe finalmente rivedere il campo. Resta da capire se dal primo minuto oppure a gara in corso. Non sarà semplice scalfire la coppia Soulé-Mora, che ha fatto molto bene durante la sua assenza, ma all'orizzonte c'è anche la sfida con il PSG e qualche rotazione potrebbe essere necessaria. Per Gasperini, comunque, si tratta di un dubbio piacevole all’orizzonte di un periodo impegnativo con tante sfide decisive ravvicinate.

Qualora dovesse trovare spazio al Tardini, l'obiettivo personale della Joya sarà anche quello di sbloccarsi in questa stagione. L'ultima rete risale infatti al 18 gennaio, in occasione di Torino-Roma 0-2. Dybala, però, conosce già bene la strada per colpire i crociati: contro il Parma ha realizzato tre gol in carriera, uno con la maglia del Palermo e due con quella giallorossa, oltre ad aver servito altrettanti assist.

#2216. Cardinale says MSE will give Milan ‘financial muscle’ and reiterates: “I will never sell”

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had launched the new holding company to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are big plans for the company.

Brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Big 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

In an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding company?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ Currently, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term…

“Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how quickly…

“My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

“Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

“We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

“No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding company?

“I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be announced at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly quickly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management company.”

Does your plan include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the company I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the New York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading…

“Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”

Gerry is right. You are wrong. Look it up.

The English Premiere League makes about FOUR TIMES as much money in TV broadcast rights as Serie A does – €4.6 billion per season (£3.84 billion – £1.68 billion domestic, £2.17 billion international).

Serie A’s TV broadcast rights give it €1.144 billion per season (€894 million domestic, €250 million international)

Total stadium revenue among all the clubs in the English Premier League is also about 2.3 x higher than total stadium revenue for all the clubs in Serie A – over £1billion per season in the EPL (€1.3 billion) compared with €435.4 million per season in Serie A.

It was not always this way. In the 1980s, English football was beset with old, rotting, unsafe stadiums, hooliganism, and low TV revenues.

In 1992, the First Division clubs broke away from the rest of the English Football League (EFL) to form the Premiere League, and began negotiating TV contracts on their own, as well as embarking on a program of enlarging and upgrading their football stadiums. The richest teams began building completely new, large modern stadiums with premium suites, etc.

Meanwhile, nothing much has changed in Italy – most of the stadiums remain municipal owned and small and old.

Ticket prices in the EPL are also generally on average about twice as expensive as in Italy.

So yeah, Serie A had its glory days in the 1990s, as wealthy magnates like Berlusconi infused their personal wealth into their clubs. I remember Fox carried Serie A football on TV in the United States back then. If you wanted to watch the English Premiere League, it was a bit of a struggle to find the matches on TV in the U.S back in the 1990s.

All that changed as the Premiere League steadily built up its international marketing and negotiated ever improved TV contracts. It began to require clubs that were promoted up to the EPL to upgrade their stadiums to meet a certain minimum seating capacity.

And so, today, when Italians complain about how Italy and Serie A can no longer compete with the English Premiere League for the best players, how the EPL hugely overpays for all its star players, the reason is that the EPL makes a $HIT TON MORE MONEY than Serie A does, across the board, in TV income (the biggest factor for the entire league), and stadium income.

That’s why Gerry wanted a new and better stadium, and why he has often talked about Serie A needing to do better marketing and improve its TV contracts.

You can’t get the best players in the world if you can’t compete financially with the richest and most watched football league in the world, which happens to be the English Premiere League right now.

Here in the US, EPL matches are carried by NBC Sports by subscription (about $130-$200 a year). NBC pays the Premiere League $450 million per season to carry English football on TV in the USA.

Serie A matches are carried by Paramount/CBS in the USA (a $90 per year subscription – it went up from $60 after the Ellison Oligarchy mergers). CBS had been paying Serie A $75.8 million per year for those TV rights. However, Serie A with its great marketing and negotiating expertise was unable to improve or renew that contract and so Serie A is currently just going year to year with CBS and getting less than $30 million a year.

Do you see the difference now in the major sources of income between the Premiere League and Serie A??

So yeah, absolutely, Gerry is right to complain about needing to get Serie A some better negotiators and marketers to improve on its TV contracts.

#2215. Approvato bilancio del Fondo di fine carriera calciatori: avanzo di 1,7 milioni

Approvato bilancio del Fondo di fine carriera calciatori: avanzo di 1,7 milioni

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Un attivo complessivo di 207,2 milioni, un avanzo di esercizio di 1.7 milioni e oltre 20,5 milioni liquidati agli iscritti nella stagione sportiva 2025/26. Sono questi i principali risultati del bilancio del Fondo di accantonamento delle indennità di fine carriera per i giocatori e allenatori di calcio, approvato oggi.

Dal 1975 a oggi, informa una nota, il Fondo ha distribuito in media più dell'84% degli avanzi generati e liquidato oltre 30.000 posizioni, riconoscendo le somme dovute ai professionisti che avevano regolarmente versato i contributi previsti. Il presidente del Fondo, Leonardo Grosso, ribadisce l'impegno dell'ente nella tutela delle somme accantonate: "I risultati del 2025/26 confermano la stabilità della gestione e, soprattutto, la capacità di assicurare con continuità le prestazioni previste". Getty Images

"Dietro ogni voce di bilancio c'è il futuro di un professionista. Per questo amministriamo le risorse con prudenza, responsabilità e una costante attenzione alla loro protezione. Gli oltre 20,5 milioni di euro corrisposti nella stagione 2025/26 rappresentano la dimostrazione concreta della nostra capacità di rispettare gli impegni assunti".

#2213. Genoa, abbondanza e dubbi per De Rossi per il Sassuolo: e al Mapei si giocherà in casa

Domenica alle 15, l'orario che piace ai tifosi e agli amanti del calcio, il Genoa tornerà in campo. Archiviata la sosta per le Nazionali, la squadra di Daniele De Rossi scenderà in campo contro il Sassuolo per mettersi alle spalle la sconfitta casalinga contro il Milan e riprendere un cammino positivo per quanto riguarda le prestazioni suffragate dalle tre vittorie di fila contro Venezia, Juventus e Lecce. Il match del Mapei Stadium di Reggio Emilia non sarà facile. Di fronte ci sarà una squadra ferita, reduce da un cambio di panchina e pronta a vendere cara la pelle.

Il mister potrà finalmente contare su una rosa completa per domenica (Venturino e Havel in settimana hanno messo minuti nelle gambe) e i dubbi sono solo legati all'abbondanza. In avanti ci sarà Milutin Osmajic reduce dal gol con la nazionale montenegrina mentre alle sue spalle Messias, Vitinha, El Shaarawy e Baldanzi si giocano due posti. Scelte anche a centrocampo con Wiafe e Traoré che potrebbero essere in vantaggio su Amorim mentre Frendrup sarà ancora da valutare. Davanti a Bijlow invece ci sarà al suo posto capitan Vasquez che tornerà fra oggi e domani dal Messico.

In terra emiliana la squadra non sarà sola. 4000 sostenitori hanno polverizzato in queste ore i tagliandi del settore ospiti e saranno pronti a spingere il Grifone a gran voce trasformando di fatto il Mapei Stadium in un piccolo "Ferraris". Per i tifosi rossoblù non ancora in possesso del biglietto per domenica è consigliato l'acquisto in Tribuna Est Laterale al prezzo di 40 euro l'intero e 30 euro il ridotto.

#2212. Watch: Camarda scores for Italy’s U21 side in 2-1 win against France

Francesco Camarda got on target for Italy’s U21 side last night as they beat France by two goals to one, bagging the opener.

It has been a tough season for Camarda so far. After a pre-season and summer that seemed to promise consistent playing time this season, the youngster has only racked up 119 minutes on the pitch between Serie A and the Europa League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

No goals have been scored either, which is obviously never ideal for a striker looking to grow. A loan move appears to be on the cards, but the January window isn’t for another month and a half, so a confidence boost cannot come quickly enough. Luckily, he got one last night.

Italy U21 played a friendly against France in Laval last night and Camarda managed to get the opener in the game. After picking up a good position, the striker veered off into the centre and found the open space in France’s defence.

Camarda received the ball from Matteo Dagasso and while it looked for a split second like the pass was overhit, he got on the end of it and found the back of the net. Once again, as we have seen with Milan this season too, his movement was crucial in creating the chance.

Let’s see what happens in the coming weeks, but perhaps he can get some more chances by Amorim and finally score his first goal with the red and black shirt.

#2209. Hristov: "Pio Esposito? Allo Spezia non parlava dell'Inter! Ma si vedeva che..."

Hristov: "Pio Esposito? Allo Spezia non parlava dell'Inter! Ma si vedeva che..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Petko Hristov, ex difensore dello Spezia oggi al Levski Sofia, intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, ha parlato così di Pio Esposito, suo compagno in Liguria: “Mostravamo i muscoli per vedere chi fosse più grosso. All’epoca vincevo sempre io. Voleva allenarsi sempre insieme a me, gli mostravo come fare alcuni esercizi. Aveva 18 anni, era il primo anno lontano dall’Inter. A fine seduta, stanchissimi, ci mettevamo davanti allo specchio per capire chi avesse lavorato di più o chi avesse fatto più pesi. Da lì a qualche settimana iniziò a esultare in quel modo”.

“Un diciottenne con la fame di arrivare, di restare un’ora in più dopo l’allenamento. Nel 2023-24 iniziai a correre con la squadra dopo tre mesi, a dicembre. Pio aveva qualche difficoltà a capire la Serie B, a trovare i giusti spazi, almeno all’inizio. Con l’arrivo di Luca D’Angelo è cambiato tutto. Nel girone di ritorno centrammo una salvezza meritata”.

Era già difficile marcarlo in partitella?

"Cavolo, sì. Lo soffrivo, ma mi piaceva. E anche a lui. Me lo diceva sempre”.

“Il suo modo di difendere il pallone e girarsi nel modo giusto. Ha tutto: tecnica, fisico, colpo di testa, quella fame che ti permette di ringhiare su ogni pallone”.

“Uguali. Ha segnato alcune volte, altre invece l'ho fermato. E poi chi segnava un gol in più esultava in faccia all’altro”.

“Riguardo il campo, poco o nulla. Solo di non discutere con gli altri compagni di squadra o di non cadere in facili provocazioni. In palestra, invece, gli dicevo come impostare gli esercizi. Per tutto il resto, c’erano l’allenatore e suo fratello Salvatore, con cui si trovava a memoria”.

“In realtà no, anzi, era straconcentrato sullo Spezia e sull'obiettivo. Nel 2024-25 segnò 19 gol. Onestamente non me l’aspettavo, anche se dopo un paio di mesi, giocando in partitella, si vedeva che rispetto all’anno prima ci fosse qualcosa di diverso. Era molto più concreto”.

“Una volta mi riaccompagnò a casa in macchina. Aveva preso da poco la patente, ci fu qualche manovra un po' così, quindi un signore dietro di noi suonò il clacson. Per scherzo, gli dissi che se fossimo scesi non ci avrebbe detto nulla. Siamo pur sempre alti più di un metro e 90…”.

“Ogni tanto sì, gli faccio i complimenti dopo ogni gol e sono fiero di ciò che sta facendo all'Inter e in Nazionale, dov'è sempre più decisivo. E' rimasto lo stesso ragazzo di La Spezia, quello che pianse sotto la curva e che tornò a salutare i suoi tifosi. Spero che mantenga questa umiltà”.

E se dovesse tornare a marcarlo? Magari in nazionale, Italia-Bulgaria…

#2208. Milan stars Pulisic and Ramos will be in action tonight – the kick-off times

Christian Pulisic and Goncalo Ramos will both be in action for their respective national sides tonight, heading into the games with different targets.

The international break isn’t exactly the most enjoyable period as a club supporter. However, the one comfort is that we can watch some of the players in action for their international sides, especially in Milan’s case as 13 players have been called up.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This evening, the likes of Pulisic (United States) and Ramos (Portugal) could get some playing time. The feeling is that they will have different targets for the games, though, given how their respective form has been with Milan.

Ramos and his Portugal will be up against Denmark in the Nations League at 20:45 CET, hoping to continue their winning run (4/4 so far). The striker himself could also score for the fourth consecutive game for his national side, which is quite a contrast from his Milan’s stats.

Indeed, after another tough period with the Rossoneri since the last break, the No.9 could use a goal or two to remind himself that he can actually find the back of the net. Let’s just hope that if he does, he brings it back to Milan as well.

For Pulisic, it’s a case of continuing the good form we have seen lately and perhaps silencing some of the national team supporters, who haven’t always gone easy on him. The USMNT are playing Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League at 22:30 CET, so it’s a late one.

#2207. Atalanta, riecco Bellanova! L'esterno scalda i motori per sfidare la sua ex Inter

Se qualcuno in queste settimane non uscirà in gruppo vista l’uscita di GTA VI, in casa Atalanta c’è sicuramente chi in gruppo è ritornato a pieno regime, con la voglia di prepararsi con gli stimoli giusti in vista della gara contro l’Inter. Stiamo parlando dell’esterno Raoul Bellanova, che da due giorni è tornato a disposizione di mister Sarri in un contesto molto particolare: si affronta la capolista, ma soprattutto quello che è stato il suo recente passato con la casacca nerazzurra milanese (prima del grande ritorno a Bergamo).

Arrivato nell’estate del 2022 dopo la grande annata fatta a Cagliari, Raoul Bellanova firma con l’Inter, dove però la titolarità non è garantita: davanti a lui sulla destra gioca Dumfries, che per Simone Inzaghi è praticamente inamovibile sulla fascia. Tuttavia, per l’attuale esterno del Real Madrid il 22/23 non è stato tra le sue migliori annate vista la troppa altalena di prestazioni, e Bellanova è sempre pronto a subentrare sebbene il minutaggio sia arrivato abbastanza con il contagocce: 22 presenze, 1 solo assist (contro il Sassuolo in casa) e zero gol, con nel mezzo una media di 30 minuti a gara tra campionato, Coppa Italia e Champions League. Un minutaggio risicato, in cui non ha saputo incidere sebbene con poco tempo a disposizione sia difficile fare la differenza.

Ora c'è l’Atalanta e la voglia di riscattare non soltanto quello che è stato il suo recente passato, ma anche la stagione scorsa (molto al di sotto delle aspettative). L’inizio di Bellanova è stato positivo con Maurizio Sarri in panchina e potrebbe addirittura ritornare dal primo minuto contro la sua ex Inter, con l’obiettivo di portare a casa un risultato importante per la Dea seppur la gara di domenica sera sia una montagna da scalare.

#2206. Lazio, mercato di gennaio: Lotito lavora da due mesi per il saldo zero

Gli agenti hanno sondato i big: il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen e la Juventus è pronta a offrire 40 milioni per Taylor.

Per la Lazio resta aperta la possibilità di operare nel mercato di gennaio a saldo zero, anziché subire un nuovo blocco totale. Lotito lavora da due mesi per trovare una soluzione. La decisione arriverà a dicembre dalla Commissione di controllo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

A settembre il blocco invernale sembrava inevitabile, dopo gli acquisti estivi e la crescita del monte ingaggi. Ora nei conti biancocelesti si intravede uno spiraglio, seppure stretto. Lotito procede senza annunci, tra trattative, incastri e verifiche dei conti; a Formello restano prudenza e speranza.

La Commissione di controllo, che ieri ha firmato un protocollo d’intesa con la Consob, darà la risposta definitiva a dicembre. Fino a quel momento, l’ipotesi del saldo zero rimane aperta, ma non è una certezza.

Nel frattempo è pronto un piano alternativo. Gli agenti hanno sondato il mercato, raccolto offerte e valutato i big della Lazio. La linea del club, però, è quella promessa a Gattuso: nessuna cessione a gennaio.

Il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen. Anche la Juventus potrebbe scontrarsi con la stessa posizione: è pronta a mettere sul tavolo 40 milioni per Taylor. La linea sulle cessioni è riassunta così: «In uscita non si muove nessuno». Almeno per ora, in attesa della decisione prevista prima di Natale.

#2202. Tare explains why Füllkrug never took off at Milan: “Injections for two months”

AC Milan’s former sporting director Igli Tare has explained that an injury most likely kept Niclas Füllkrug from taking off at AC Milan, scoring just one goal.

It was at the start of January of this year that Milan decided to bring in Füllkrug to bolster the No.9 position for the second half of the season. While the start was encouraging on the pitch, with the winner against Lecce on January 18, he never really took off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Actually, if you knew what was going on behind the scenes, the start wasn’t even that encouraging. Just over a week or so after joining, he broke his toe and it ended up having a huge effect on the entire loan spell.

Speaking to Sky Sport last night, Milan’s former sporting director Tare was asked about the signing of Füllkrug. This season, the German has scored 12 goals in 11 games for Werder Bremen and the director believes he could have had those numbers for the Rossoneri without the injury.

Füllkrug performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

“It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund,” he stated.

#2201. "Un giorno tornerò". Conte riaccende la Juve, ma oggi non si fa, parola di Romano

Basta una frase per far tremare i polsi al popolo bianconero e rimettere in moto la macchina del calciomercato, le parole pronunciate da Antonio Conte ai microfoni di Cronache di Spogliatoio ("Un giorno la mia storia con la Juventus chiuderà il cerchio") hanno immediatamente infiammato l'ambiente, alimentando le fantasie di un clamoroso ritorno a Torino. A fare chiarezza tra suggestioni e realtà ci ha pensato tra gli altri Fabrizio Romano, che sul proprio canale YouTube ha fotografato con precisione come a suo dire, stanno le cose.

Nonostante il momento delicato attraversato dalla squadra, dalla Continassa non è partito alcun segnale verso l'allenatore leccese, non ci sono stati contatti diretti né indiretti tra la dirigenza juventina e l'entourage di Conte. Nessuna telefonata esplorativa, nessuna trattativa sotto traccia, il tecnico, attualmente libero sul mercato, non ha mai nascosto la sua disponibilità a valutare un progetto ambizioso e a lungo termine, mettendo l'aspetto tecnico davanti a quello economico, ma per tornare alla Juve servirebbero condizioni ben precise che oggi non sono sul tavolo.

Il motivo principale di questa calma piatta sul fronte Conte ha un nome e un cognome: Luciano Spalletti. Il club bianconero, pur consapevole dell'importanza cruciale dei prossimi impegni stagionali per il futuro della panchina, continua a blindare il proprio allenatore. La linea della dirigenza, ribadita anche da Giovanni Carnevali, è quella della continuità e della fiducia nell'attuale guida tecnica.

Resta dunque una finestra aperta sul futuro, alimentata dal sentimento mai sopito di Conte per i colori con cui ha scritto pagine indimenticabili da giocatore e da allenatore, ma tra il desiderio di "chiudere il cerchio" e una firma sul contratto c'è di mezzo il presente, oggi la Juventus guarda avanti con Spalletti, mentre Conte attende la chiamata giusta per tornare in pista.

#2198. Cardinale says pre-season is ‘up to Amorim’ as Milan will not chase ‘extra two million’

Gerry Cardinale has provided some refreshing comments on Milan’s pre-season plans for the future, confirming that money will no longer dictate where they go.

Over the last ten years or so, it has become far more common for big clubs to travel across the world for their pre-season campaigns. For example, Milan have been in Australia for two consecutive pre-seasons now, taking on Perth Glory and most recently Inter.

While it’s great to connect with local fan bases, the travel is demanding for the players. This summer, Milan played games in Glasgow (Scotland), Perth (Australia), Jakarta (Indonesia), and Wroclaw (Poland). resulting in a lot of travel.

Speaking about the pre-season in his long interview with Gazzetta dello Sport, Cardinale said that the upcoming pre-season planning will be decided by Ruben Amorim. Money will no longer dictate where they go. Instead, the best plan for preparing the players will be chosen.

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

That would be a HUGE step if so and I’d be impressed if we chose to. This pre season we really lacked tests against the sort of teams we were going to be playing in the first few games, because we were playing the biggest names we could sign up. Hopefully a nice balance can be struck.

Under previous management? Who is he kidding right now? Horrible stuff, how disgraceful, unethical & unbecoming. Amnesia is a bi*ch.

I don’t know if they were, or weren’t, but it’s one possibility to explain what he is saying. The other possibility is that he is referring to Furlani. Remember, Furlani was the previous ownership’s man and got imposed on the current ownership due to corporate monitoring while the current ownership owed money to the previous one, under the vendor’s loan. I’m very glad that Gerry refinanced the loan elsewere and kicked out Furlani.

I think that at this point, I am granting to Gerry the benefit of the doubt. Sure, we still need to see results and consistency to actually give him a pass, but the signs are positive.

But I think it can’t be denied that things are looking better now than in the previous four years. Let’s allow ourselves to have some hope. Again, this said, if then it is revealed that his promises are empty, I will put to rest my willingness to temporarily give him the benefit of the doubt, and will turn against him again.

elliott management. they left in june when gerry refinanced the loan. hence why furlani left. he was elliott guy looking after elliott investment.

Yes. And in any case, it takes a little time to fully take over a large organization. There is a learning curve, and Gerry does not have a football background. Perhaps he really is learning things. Also note that he’s basically confirming Amorim for next season, no matter what happens in the standings (barring a relegation battle of course). This is also a big deal. Maybe he knew the mistake he did previous years but remember he not the sole owner then but in partnership with previous owner. He can’t really decide what happened due to some circumstances, and I’m supporting him with the desire and fire 🔥 I found in his heart ❤️. Let make Milan a better team

#2197. Lazio, mercato: Fabiani riattiva la talent room, Lang tra i nomi

Le priorità sono una mezz’ala e un vice Zaccagni; per l’esterno destro lo sguardo è rivolto a giugno.

Fabiani ha rimesso in moto la talent room della Lazio. Secondo Il Messaggero, gli svincolati non convincono: la ricerca riguarda giovani, occasioni e profili per i quali servono risorse. Il lavoro prosegue come se il mercato fosse ancora possibile, o per farsi trovare pronti nel caso in cui lo diventasse.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Le esigenze immediate sono una mezz’ala e un vice Zaccagni. La ricerca di un esterno destro guarda invece a giugno, quando scadrà il contratto di Cancellieri.

Fra i nomi seguiti ci sono Ebu Bekir Is, classe 2008 dell’Eintracht, e Marco Brescianini della Fiorentina. Sono profili inseriti nella ricerca avviata da Fabiani, che non si concentra sui calciatori svincolati.

Il nome che accende maggiormente l’interesse è Noa Lang, protagonista contro la Lazio al Maradona. Il giocatore piace molto sul piano tecnico, mentre restano perplessità legate all’aspetto caratteriale.

Arrivare a Lang a gennaio è comunque difficile. La pista potrebbe invece prendere forza in estate, nell’ambito dei nomi valutati per il mercato biancoceleste.

#2196. Roma, oltre Endrick c’è anche Nusa nella lista dei desideri. Il Lipsia apre?

Continua la ricerca dell’esterno d’attacco per la Roma. I giallorossi non mollano di un centimetro tutte le piste di livello, anche perché la sensazione è quella di poter rimanere in lotta per lo scudetto fino al termine della stagione. E per questo serve un acquisto top.

E se Endrick rimane la prima scelta (anche se la concorrenza è davvero tanta a partire da quella del Milan), Tony D’Amico continua a sondare anche altri terreni. Un’altra bella soluzione sarebbe Nusa, un giocatore di altissima qualità in grado di spostare gli equilibri. Il Lipsia a gennaio non è intenzionato a prendere in considerazione l’ipotesi di cederlo. L’esplosione di El Ayanoui, che è diventato titolare inamovibile però potrebbe essere di aiuto alla Roma. Il club tedesco può riscattarlo a giugno per la cifra di 25 milioni di euro dai giallorossi. E questo potrebbe essere un appiglio in più per allargare la trattativa a Nusa. Il discorso è complicatissimo ma non impossibile.

Intanto un altro profilo che è entrato nei radar dei giallorossi è Scherhant, esterno di piede destro molto bravo a giocare a sinistra in forza al Friburgo. Sempre da non trascurare anche l’opzione Lewelling dello Stoccarda, che la Roma nell’ultima estate è stata ad un passo da acquistare. Restano vive anche le piste che portano a Gittens del Chelsea e Kvernadze del Frosinone. Insomma la Roma non si ferma un attimo e presto alzerà il pressing per regalare il giocatore giusto per rafforzare l’attacco.

"I giocatori della Lazio fanno quello che sanno fare e quindi ad ora viaggiano. Lo scudetto è una grande scommessa e illusione, ma capisco l'entusiasmo dei tifosi, perché una stagione in cui le altre non danno il cento per cento può capitare. Ad ora non vedo troppe squadre che possono metterla in difficoltà, ma sicuramente capiremo di più quando avrà affrontato Roma, Inter e Como. In questo momento sono sulle ali dell'entusiasmo".

#2194. Lazio, Lotito e il mercato: le mosse segrete

L'accordo tecnico c'è, ma Mizuno può pareggiare l'offerta danese, superiore ai cinque milioni a stagione.

Lotito ha ottenuto una proroga per dilazionare le vecchie imposte degli anni del Covid, che pesavano per molti milioni sulla liquidità della Lazio. Secondo Il Messaggero, il presidente prova ora ad anticipare i crediti futuri degli sponsor e a inserirli nella documentazione per la Commissione, nel tentativo di trovare risorse per il mercato.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La dilazione delle imposte alleggerisce un peso sulla liquidità del club. Il passo successivo a cui lavora Lotito riguarda i crediti legati alle future sponsorizzazioni: anticiparli potrebbe trasformarli in risorse da presentare alla Commissione.

Il presidente ha cercato diverse soluzioni, ma non ha certezze e non vuole alimentare aspettative. Non ne ha parlato neppure con Gattuso, per evitare di illudere il tecnico.

Per Hummel il discorso è distinto da quello dei crediti degli sponsor. L'accordo tecnico c'è, ma occorre attendere che Mizuno rinunci alla prelazione che le consentirebbe di pareggiare l'offerta danese, superiore ai cinque milioni a stagione.

La situazione resta quindi legata alla scelta di Mizuno. Lotito, intanto, mantiene il silenzio anche su questo fronte.

#2193. Pinamonti e la prima da titolare in casa: Lazio-Lecce per il tris

Senza Zaccagni, Gattuso prepara Noslin sulla sinistra; Frattesi si è allenato in gruppo, ma resta il dubbio sul suo impiego.

Andrea Pinamonti giocherà per la prima volta da titolare all’Olimpico con la Lazio nella sfida di sabato contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, L’assenza di Zaccagni gli darà ancora spazio al centro dell’attacco, con Noslin sulla sinistra al posto del capitano. Per il centravanti è un’occasione per cercare il terzo gol in biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Pinamonti sa di non aver ancora conquistato i tifosi laziali. La fiducia di Gattuso nei suoi confronti, racconta La Repubblica, alimenta però la sua voglia di riscatto e può aiutarlo a sbloccarsi anche dal primo minuto.

Nelle due precedenti gare iniziate da titolare, a Udine e Napoli, il numero 9 arrivato in estate non ha convinto. È stato sostituito nella ripresa, rispettivamente al 52’ e al 61’. Sabato spera che la prima partenza dall’inizio in casa segni un cambiamento.

Proprio all’Olimpico, entrando nel secondo tempo, ha segnato i suoi due gol con la Lazio. Il colpo di testa contro il Cagliari è stato decisivo; il piattone del 3-1 contro il Monza ha chiuso una partita rimasta fino a quel momento in bilico. Ora Pinamonti va a caccia del tris.

Contro il Lecce, Noslin prenderà il posto di Zaccagni sulla fascia sinistra, mentre Pinamonti agirà al centro. L’intesa tra l’attaccante italiano e l’olandese è ancora da affinare, ma Gattuso è convinto che la formula possa funzionare.

Il tecnico ha ricevuto segnali positivi anche da Frattesi. La mezzala ha svolto con il gruppo il primo allenamento settimanale. Il lavoro in squadra non scioglie ancora la riserva su un suo impiego dal primo minuto contro il Lecce, ma cresce l’ottimismo sulla sua presenza.

#2191. Tuttosport: Stuttgart midfielder back on Milan’s radar amid imminent Krösche arrival

AC Milan are evaluating several players for the midfield in the hope of finding Luka Modric’s heir, with a previous target re-emerging on their radar.

Modric renewed his contract with Milan in the summer and has been performing well so far, certainly showing that age still isn’t an issue for him. In fact, he has even said that as long as he feels like he does right now, there is no reason to retire.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That said, Milan are obviously thinking about what life could be without the veteran. Ardon Jashari was perhaps initially identified as his heir, but his struggles so far and characteristics suggest someone else might arrive for that role.

According to today’s edition of Tuttosport, as transcribed by MilanNews, the likes of Yasin Ayari (Brighton) and Alex Scott (Bournemouth) are two players on Milan’s radar. However, with the arrival of Markus Krösche as the new Head of Football, another name could go to the top of the list.

We are talking about Stuttgart’s Angelo Stiller, who was linked with a move to the Rossoneri at the end of 2024 as well. The 25-year-old has a €40m release clause in his contract and several big clubs are keeping an eye on him.

It’s still very early, of course, as Krösche hasn’t even officially joined the club yet, but the German midfielder at least appears to be back in the fold.

#2188. CorSport: Fontanella-Khan up and running within Milan’s management – his background and role

James Fontanella-Khan is up and running with his new position at AC Milan, following an interesting background which includes the former Rossoneri man Alberto Gilardino.

It was in the middle of September that various outlets reported that Fontanella-Khan was joining Milan’s management as the new Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. Two months have passed since and the 43-year-old is now up and running with his new gig.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He has been spotted among the top brass in the stands of San Siro during the most recent games and he was also present at the dinner Gerry Cardinale hosted before the derby. In other words, he’s not exactly working remotely, instead expected to spend most of his time in Milan.

Today’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) has taken a closer look at Fontanella-Khan, who has various valuable experiences to rely on in his new gig. Most recently, he was the US Financial Editor for the Financial Times, even moderating some conferences that Cardinale spoke at.

Before making waves in the US, however, he actually grew up in Italy and even played football himself. He was a goalkeeper in Piacenza’s youth team, reaching the Primavera of the club, and he was even a teammate of Alberto Gilardino (the former Milan striker) at one point.

After deciding that football wasn’t his path in life, he left Italy to start an internship for the Financial Times in London. He worked his way up and remained at the newspaper for over 20 years before accepting the Milan gig.

As for his role with Milan, according to Corriere dello Sport, he could be described as a General Manager. He handles communications, politics (he will be present at the League assemblies), and represents the club at various events.

Part of his goal is to connect the US mentality of the Rossoneri ownership with the Italian identity of the club, partly relying on his background as a footballer and Milan fan.

#2186. Serie A, chi rientra dopo la sosta e gli squalificati del turno

Gudmundsson è atteso contro il Lecce; Bracaglia e Ndiaye devono fermarsi per una giornata, così come il tecnico Juric.

Gudmundsson è atteso contro il Lecce e Rovella torna tra le opzioni a disposizione della Lazio. È uno dei recuperi nel quadro della Serie A aggiornato alla mattina del 18 novembre 2026, in vista della dodicesima giornata in programma dal 21 al 23 novembre. Secondo quanto riportato da DAZN, Tra gli squalificati del turno figurano Gabriele Bracaglia del Frosinone e Ndiaye del Parma; deve fermarsi per una giornata anche l’allenatore del Monza Ivan Juric.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La sosta ha restituito alle squadre alcuni giocatori, lasciando aperte altre valutazioni dopo gli impegni con le Nazionali. Le finestre di rientro restano indicative e le convocazioni per il prossimo turno non sono ancora definitive.

Gudmundsson ha completato il recupero ed è atteso per la partita contro il Lecce. Anche Rovella rientra tra le opzioni a disposizione.

Tra gli altri recuperi, Bellanova e Raspadori sono tornati ad allenarsi in gruppo il 17 novembre e sono attesi tra i disponibili contro l’Inter. Mina e Obert hanno svolto parte della seduta con la squadra, mentre Nzola, Aurelio e Trepy hanno ripreso il lavoro collettivo e si avvicinano al ritorno tra i convocati. Resta da confermare la disponibilità di Sugamele, già segnalato alle prese con un problema fisico.

Chalobah è atteso a disposizione contro il Cagliari. Liberali ha superato l’infortunio, ma il suo impiego è ancora da verificare. Va valutata anche la piena disponibilità di Ranieri dopo il problema al piede. Gabriele Bracaglia, invece, salterà il Milan per una giornata di squalifica.

Nell’ultimo aggiornamento sull’infermeria rossoblù, Frendrup è indicato come unico indisponibile. Venturino non compare più tra le assenze segnalate.

In casa Inter, Lautaro Martinez e Marcus Thuram si sono allenati con il gruppo il 17 novembre. Gli esami di Akanji hanno dato esito negativo dopo l’affaticamento accusato con la Svizzera; il suo rientro ad Appiano è previsto il 18 novembre. I fastidi al piede di Zielinski non destano particolare preoccupazione, ma saranno ricontrollati al ritorno dalla Nazionale.

Cambiaso, Celik e Nico Gonzalez hanno lavorato a parte anche il 17 novembre e restano in dubbio. Cambiaso è alle prese con un affaticamento alla coscia, Celik con un fastidio accusato in Nazionale; Gonzalez sta recuperando dal problema al soleo. Zhegrova ha ripreso parte del lavoro con il gruppo, mentre Conceição ha superato il problema alla spalla ed è tornato ad allenarsi con la squadra.

Berisha ha ripreso il lavoro con i compagni: il sovraccarico muscolare non lo colloca più tra le assenze certe. Per Maignan, gli esami del 17 novembre non hanno evidenziato lesioni nella regione pubo-adduttoria. Il portiere resta monitorato, ma può essere disponibile contro il Frosinone. Pavlovic ha ripreso parzialmente il lavoro in gruppo e punta alla convocazione; Terracciano è ancora da valutare dopo il trauma alla spalla.

Non sono uniformi le ricostruzioni disponibili su Ziolkowski, Pessina, Ciurria, Mout e Ngonge, presenti nelle precedenti segnalazioni. Non vengono quindi considerati assenze certe: per la loro situazione farà fede l’aggiornamento del club prima delle convocazioni. L’allenatore del Monza Ivan Juric deve scontare una giornata di squalifica.

Neres, Favasuli e Spinazzola hanno ripreso almeno parte delle sedute con la squadra e puntano alla convocazione contro il Torino. Per loro non sono più attuali le precedenti indicazioni di assenza certa fino alla fine di novembre o a dicembre.

#2184. Donare sangue, un gesto da campioni: Patrizio Oliva ad Aversa per una mattinata di donazioni

Un gesto di solidarietà che può fare la differenza. Sabato 21 novembre, dalle 9 alle 13, il Center Union di Aversa, in Viale Kennedy 35, ospiterà “Dona, fai la differenza”, iniziativa promossa da Union Gas e Luce in collaborazione con la Casa del Donatore di Aversa per sensibilizzare sull’importanza della donazione del sangue.

All’evento parteciperà anche Patrizio Oliva, campione olimpico di pugilato e testimonial di Union, che incontrerà i partecipanti e sosterrà la campagna di sensibilizzazione. «Non serve essere campioni per fare un gesto da campioni», è il messaggio lanciato dall’ex pugile. L’iniziativa si inserisce nell’impegno di Union a favore del territorio e della responsabilità sociale, con l’obiettivo di coinvolgere cittadini, associazioni e realtà locali nella promozione della cultura della donazione. «L’energia più bella è quella che condividiamo», il messaggio che accompagna l’evento.

#2182. Gila discusses his mental health journey, perfectionism and current state: “Changed my perspective”

In the latest episode of AC Milan’s The Chamber series, Mario Gila was the guest and spoke about the positive mental health journey that he’s currently on.

It was last month that Milan unveiled their new series, called The Chamber, which focuses on the mental health of the players at the club. Luka Modric was the first guest, a perfect start in many ways, and the second episode has now been published with Mario Gila as the guest.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The concept, in case you’re not familiar, is that the players are placed in a ‘Chamber’ with no outside noise for a few minutes. Then, they are interviewed by the host Luca Casadei, who focuses on the mental state of the players.

As said, Gila was the guest in the most recent edition and he has a lot to say, having been on a mental health journey in the last few years. Indeed, after hitting ‘rock-bottom’ at Lazio, he found a way through and is now very happy.

How are you feeling right now? [after being in the chamber, editor’s note]

I feel very peaceful, I feel really good here. I think experiences like this are also closely linked to how a person feels and where they are emotionally at that moment. And I think it amplifies everything… a little. I wanted to experience it to the fullest when they told me about it.

I think when there are no outside influences clouding your mind that’s when you connect most with yourself. That’s why I closed my eyes. I wanted to feel as deeply as possible what was inside me and how my mind works in moments like this.”

What did you feel during this experience?

Well, I really enjoyed it because I felt so peaceful. I felt completely at ease, and it was an experience I’ve rarely had before. I’m someone who likes to meditate, to reconnect with myself, and I’m interested in spirituality, it’s something I genuinely enjoy.

“And I felt so much peace, so much peace because with everything so quiet, such complete silence and being in touch with myself, it really is an experience I’m not sure I’ll ever forget. I really liked it.”

Speaking about yourself, are there moments when you’re alone, away from the public eye, away from everyone expecting something of you, when you take some time just for yourself? I’d like to know what you feel, who you are emotionally in those moments.

It doesn’t happen to me often because, whether you like it or not, footballers tend to have very active minds. It’s a profession that takes a huge mental toll.

“But I try, for example, during holidays or whenever we get some time off, to find situations where I feel, well, maybe not exactly like in that chamber, but where I can connect with myself, where I can rediscover that Mario who sometimes gets a little lost because of the job he does.

“And in those moments, well, I feel at peace, I feel that connection with myself, I feel like a person. Because in our profession, whether we like it or not, we lose touch with ourselves a little. And that’s what I’m trying to achieve when I’m alone with myself.”

You told me that because of the job you do, you’re always very focused. I wanted to talk about control because I’ve heard you say you need to have everything under control.

Yes, I think that, given the way I see the profession and the position we footballers are in, I think it may not seem like it, but you have a lot of things to manage. How you behave off the pitch, you’re a footballer 24 hours a day, your diet, physical preparation, training sessions, the physio.

And it’s like… I have to keep everything perfectly under control so that at the weekend or in a midweek match I’m at my best.  So the profession itself pushes you to keep everything under control and if you’re also someone who likes that and believes things should be that way, you take it even further.

“And in those situations, I feel comfortable when everything’s under control.”

Is that just at work, or does it apply everywhere, with your family, your friends, always needing to have everything under control?

I’ve been like that with my family too, with my teammates, with my friends, but I see my personal life differently now. I didn’t before. Because perfection is exhausting.  In the end, so many expectations… Striving for perfection wears you out.

“I think that, to a certain extent, it’s boring. You don’t get to see the real person, their authentic self. So that’s how I’ve been for much of my life. I’m young, but I’ve been like that. Now I’m beginning to understand better that everyone is different, that every moment is different, and to appreciate that more, that authenticity.

Did you used to feel weak when you weren’t in control? Vulnerable?

Now, though, you’ve realised it’s a strength?

“Yes, yes, yes. I understand that people and situations aren’t always as we want or expect them to be. And I think it’s somewhat connected to ego, but now we’re getting into some pretty deep territory. But…I like it! I think so, yes, I used to be like that. I used to be. I’m less like that now, and I appreciate difficult moments more because there’s also a lot of good to be found in those moments.

“I mean, we can’t control everything, we can’t expect everything to be perfect because perfection doesn’t teach you anything. I don’t think there’s anything particularly positive about it.

“In the end, we grow a lot through… or we become stronger during difficult times than during good ones. So I’ve largely let go of that kind of perfectionism. And those incredibly high expectations, I don’t like them anymore.”

But is there a positive side to perfectionism for you? Do you think you became the player you are thanks to your perfectionism?

“Yes. This is a struggle I have with myself, for example. In this profession, I believe that perfectionism and ego are two things that drive us to succeed at work, in our professional lives. Ego drives you to be better than, say, the opponent you’re playing against.

“Perfectionism makes you work harder, train better, take better care of yourself and I think that helps you develop a lot professionally. But there has to be a balance. It can’t all be about perfectionism because it makes you incredibly demanding of yourself and when you go through difficult times, you won’t know how to deal with them.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

This interview is also meant to share some values with others, right? In those moments, what exactly do you tell yourself to be kinder to yourself?

“Well… What a good question! In moments when I’ve gone through difficult situations, perhaps, after that period I was telling you about, I’m aware that everyone can make mistakes. I know that making mistakes is part of the job and it’s what helps me grow.

“So I changed my perspective. I used to see it very negatively, now I find the positive in the negative. So I understand that if I focus on something positive or look at it from a positive perspective, everything surrounding the mistake changes.

“All that noise stops being noise and turns into a sense of calm. It’s normal to make a mistake and be demanding of yourself, to want to avoid making that mistake again, but it might still happen.

“So at that moment, I believe that being kind to yourself and recognising that it’s something that can happen and that you can use it to improve, is, I think, the way forward to avoid falling into negativity. But instead maintain that positivity and balance that can help you feel at peace, as I was saying in there, like the experience I had in there earlier.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

Today, with the maturity and mindset you’ve developed, how do you handle pressure? Those moments when expectations are high, when your heart starts beating faster, how do you deal with those moments?

“It depends. Because speaking for myself, I see pressure as something that helps give me that extra push to… I mean, I’m someone who believes that footballers naturally feel pressure or feel a little nervous before a match, even the day before, depending on the match, some matches are more important than others, but you still feel that pressure.

“I think accepting that pressure is positive because it helps prepare you, but I haven’t had situations where pressure has paralysed me, because I experienced that in the past.

“In the past, I’ve felt that kind of pressure, and pressure that paralyses you is very negative because it’s very different from the pressure you feel when you’re in a good place mentally, which helps you prepare.

“It’s a kind of pressure, the pressure I used to feel, that completely paralyses you, it’s a pressure that makes your heart race, that makes you afraid, so they’re two different kinds of pressure. I’ve experienced both.

“The first is difficult to handle because it’s anxiety, the expectation of performing well, it’s the feeling that so many people are watching you, you have to perform well, you have to play well, and that gets into your head, and I don’t think it’s very positive.

“The other, on the other hand, helps you prepare, you feel a little nervous, you get that slight feeling of getting yourself ready, but if you manage to channel it properly, it becomes something that prepares you, a natural response to having something important to face.”

Listening to you speak and watching you play, I see someone who’s very composed. That confidence you have in yourself, have you always had it? Where does it come from?

“I’m someone who has always given the impression of being very confident. I mean, I’ve always believed I had a lot of confidence in myself, but actually, when things got tough, I didn’t have it because whenever I went through a difficult time, I doubted myself a lot.

“I think you develop that through psychological work, but also by feeling confident in your work. Those things go hand in hand. I mean, it’s not all down to the psychologist and nothing to do with my career.

“No. I mean, everything has gone hand in hand. When I started going through this process, things also started going really well for me in football, which helped along the way. So I’ve managed to develop confidence in both areas, which has made me the person I am today, someone who I believe really does have a lot of confidence in himself, because I genuinely feel it.

“It’s something I’ve worked on a lot, learning to believe in yourself, not because of what other people say or the value others place on you, but because of the value you give yourself. And that’s where I’ve found my stability, my peace and my confidence in that environment.

You’ve played alongside some incredible players. How did you manage… I mean, did you use the comparison with their talent as a way to grow rather than feeling envious, as something positive to help you improve?

“Yes. The thing is, this is very closely connected to confidence. You know? When you believe in yourself and have that confidence, you learn to appreciate what you can learn from others. If you’re perhaps someone who doesn’t have much confidence in yourself, you might feel envious of others.

“And then you fail to recognise the lesson that the other person is teaching you, even when you can learn just by watching them. So I began to understand that when I started reaching a place of emotional wellbeing, where I was more focused on the present.

“Before, because I had less confidence in myself, I compared myself to others more. Maybe I didn’t appreciate what someone else was doing or perhaps I couldn’t fully appreciate what they were trying to teach me.

“Once you manage to build a solid sense of confidence and truly believe in yourself, you see what others can teach you in a positive light. And you see it as an opportunity to grow, you look at it from a different perspective.

“So it’s not just about what people might be teaching you directly. I’ve learned from many players just by watching, just by paying attention. But sometimes I’ve learned from negative things too. I mean, not just from positive things. I understand that learning isn’t just about someone saying: ‘Listen, you need to do this, and I think you should do it this way’.

“No, it’s also about how they behave. For example, right now we have Luka Modric in the team. And I pay a lot of attention to him, to how he behaves, to the humility he shows, to how he handles different situations.

“And that’s something you understand when you’re comfortable with yourself. If you’re not comfortable with yourself, I don’t think you’ll be able to understand that. I mean, you won’t see the other person as a positive example. You’ll see them in a negative light.

And when you’re experiencing a great moment, are you able to recognise it? To feel proud of yourself? To enjoy that moment of happiness? To stop and appreciate it?

“That’s something I struggle with, for example. It’s something I find difficult because I’m aware of it, but I think it’s something that people generally struggle with because we tend to notice the negative things more or give more importance to difficult moments than to the positive ones.

“And I think that’s a mistake everyone makes, I don’t know why. But I’m trying to work on it, I’m aware of it. But I have to tell you that if we were to compare how much I enjoy the good moments with how much I suffer during the bad ones, no.

“I suffer more during the bad moments than I enjoy the good ones. And unfortunately, that’s something I still haven’t learned how to manage or how to truly enjoy those positive moments because we’re also here to enjoy the good moments and to experience them fully. But I find that harder than dealing with a difficult moment.”

I really like how much you’ve grown in terms of maturity, everything you’ve come to understand. So I’d like to ask you one last question to reflect on everything. It’s a simple question: How are you?

Not how you are today, but looking at your life, what kind of chapter are you going through right now? Is Mario happy?

Mario is very happy. I mean, this whole conversation we’ve had has a lot to do with the positive place I’m in right now. If I were going through a difficult time, perhaps there are many things I wouldn’t understand the way I do now.

“But I’m in a really good place right now because I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m somewhere I’m appreciated and loved. I became a father a year ago. I have a wife who loves me very much too.

“It’s as though so many things are coming together, things are going well in my career, things are going well with my family. I have friends who I believe are truly valuable people. I also have a family that means so much to me.

“So it’s like everything is going really well right now. So I feel very balanced, I feel very much at peace. I feel like I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m really appreciated. So right now I’m at a very happy point in my life. Very happy.

“If negative things happen, I have a support system I can rely on. I have that support that helps me feel okay. And I think that’s really important because I believe you’ll always experience difficult moments in life. So there’s no way to completely avoid those difficult moments, you can’t, it’s just not possible.

“And life would lose its meaning. But having that safety net and that support system, I think it also allows you to thrive in every other area of your life. So I’m very happy. Right now I feel incredibly happy, very peaceful, very balanced, very happy with myself too, and I’m genuinely very happy we had this conversation because I’m really interested in all these psychological aspects,” he concluded.
