#2133. Leandro Rinaudo: "Napoli, ti manca Conte. Frosinone pazzesco. Palermo, vai in A"

Voglia di tornare dopo l’impresa con il Mantova dello scorso anno, una rivoluzione che ha portato la squadra a conquistare una salvezza che sembrava utopia. Ma senza fretta. Leandro Rinaudo, direttore sportivo, risponderà presente alla prossima chiamata soltanto se sentirà le giuste vibrazioni. Le stesse che hanno portato il Mantova, la scorsa stagione, a mantenere la categoria. Il dirigente intanto si gode gli affetti più cari e chiaramente programma il futuro. Gira, guarda partite, tesse relazioni. Aspettando le sensazioni giuste. La location è Mondello, La Sirenetta, simbolo della borgata marinara. La temperatura è ancora tra primavera ed estate, è pomeriggio e fa buio già alle 17.30, il calendario infatti dice novembre. Anche se la temperatura a Palermo racconta altro. Due poltrone, un pianoforte dietro a fare da cornice e il mare alle spalle. Leandro Rinaudo si concede a TuttoMercatoWeb.com, spaziando su vari temi. Dal calcio italiano che deve ripartire al campionato, con un occhio al futuro. Vibes, appunto, permettendo.

Rinaudo, l'Italia è fuori anche dalla Nations League. Però questa volta l'uscita di scena sembra meno amara. "I segnali sono stati comunque positivi, soprattutto nella prima parte. C'è stato un ricambio generazionale, con calciatori che arrivavano anche da campionati diversi. Purtroppo non abbiamo portato l'evento più importante, che è la qualificazione. Quindi s'è tornati al punto di partenza, ma con basi diverse per poter ripartire e riaprire un nuovo ciclo e iniziare un bel percorso. Sì, l'uscita è meno amara. Anche se dà continuità a diverse mancate qualificazioni e resta l'alone negativo che c'è sull'Italia. Però se guardiamo la proposta di calcio, l'impiego di alcuni calciatori giovani, le convocazioni di calciatori di altri campionati, si stanno gettando le basi per tornare ad essere l'Italia che eravamo abituati a vedere".

Ci fanno ben sperare i prospetti delle nazionali giovanili. "C'è del materiale importante. Il lavoro che sta facendo Silvio Baldini è importantissimo sul piano dell'espressione del gioco. Sta valorizzando tanti talenti. L'Under 21 è il serbatoio principale per il futuro dell'Italia".

Torna il campionato. E la Lazio è prima in classifica. "Meritatamente. È bello vedere un allenatore che ha sempre avuto la forza di reagire e mettersi in discussione godersi il primato e raccogliere ciò che merita dimostrando sul campo".

Anche il Frosinone di Alvini e Castagnini è una bella favola. "Pazzesco. L'anno scorso ho toccato con mano la realtà, li ho affrontati di presenza. Renzo Castagnini è stato bravissimo come sempre con le sue scoperte. E Alvini sta dimostrando di essere un allenatore importante con delle idee rivoluzionarie per quello che è il calcio di oggi. Questo Frosinone è una bella realtà e spero che centri il traguardo finale".

Che succede al suo ex Napoli? "Sta vivendo un momento negativo, l'assenza di Conte si sta vedendo. Napoli negli ultimi anni ha raggiunto obiettivi importanti come proprietà e come squadra. Quest'anno sta facendo fatica, serve tempo".

Va a corrente alternata anche la Juventus. "Credo che sia ancora alla ricerca dell'asset giusto. Ha avuto dei problemi in passato e oggi è alla ricerca anche dell'equilibrio economico, ma è la Juve e deve vincere. Una serie di situazioni che deve essere messa a posto, sicuramente Spalletti ha conosciuto meglio i suoi calciatori ma non è facile: quando equilibrio economico e mercato devono coincidere è più complicato, ma la proprietà della Juventus è talmente forte che non ha bisogno di consigli. E poi c'è Giovanni Carnevali che è l'uomo giusto per tracciare la strada e raggiungere risultati importanti".

Per il Palermo la strada sembra tracciata, verso la Serie A. "Quest'anno è stato costruito per vincere ad ogni costo, ad ogni modo, con giocatori esperti che hanno qualità per poter risolvere le partite anche quando non si mettono per il verso giusto. Inzaghi ha trovato l'alchimia giusta anche con la gente. S'è creata l'atmosfera giusta per raggiungere l'obiettivo. Arriveranno dei momenti negativi come è normale che sia, ma ci sono tutte le condizioni per arrivare all'obiettivo".

Chi è oggi l'antagonista del Palermo? "Ogni anno ci sono sempre due-tre squadre che dettano legge sul campionato di B e dimostrano il giusto spessore per arrivare in fondo. Il Palermo sta dimostrando che è l'unica regina. Le tre retrocesse stanno facendo fatica, ma vedo risvegli importanti sul piano dell'autostima e la proposta di calcio: mi riferisco a Cremonese, Pisa e Verona. E il Modena è una squadra che se trova la continuità di risultati per profondità di rosa e caratteristiche potrebbe essere la sorpresa".

E il Mantova? Lei l'anno scorso ha rivoluzionato la squadra e l'ha portata alla salvezza. "L'anno scorso è stato fatto un gran bel lavoro. Se mi guardo indietro credo che sia stata un'impresa difficile da ripetere. Sono arrivati dei risultati importanti. Questo Mantova ha dei valori e può fare molto bene anche quest'anno, devo fare i complimenti al Presidente Piccoli".

Pronto a tornare in pista? Magari in una situazione meno burrascosa... "L'idea di lavorare c'è sempre. Non è retorica, ma è normale vedere partite, relazionarsi con le persone che fanno parte del calcio. Ho la possibilità per migliorare il mio inglese e il mio sistema di lavoro tra database e intelligenza artificiale usata in un certo modo. Aspetto l'opportunità giusta, soprattutto dopo il lavoro dell'anno scorso".

Per ogni appassionato di calcio c'è una data cerchiata in rosso: il 14 dicembre. Verrà eletto il presidente federale, è sfida tra Galliani e Malagò. "Un momento importante per definire la via, la strada del calcio italiano per il presente e il futuro. Il buonsenso e l'esperienza di alcune persone di questo spessore indirizzeranno la strada giusta per l'Italia, che merita un presente e un futuro importante. Ci aspettiamo di tornare al Mondiale, manca da tanto tempo. Ma alcuni eventi nella vita avvengono per fare sì che qualcosa di forte e profondo ci faccia ragionare e trovare la via giusta".

#2132. Barnsley vs Sheffield Wednesday predictions lodged as the Tykes ‘saddening’ decline continues

Barnsley come into Friday’s Yorkshire derby against Sheffield Wednesday in dire straits. The Tykes sit 23rd in the League One table with just nine points to their name after seven defeats in their last nine matches in the third tier.

Daniel Stendel‘s side had found some respite in domestic competition with wins over Aldershot Town and Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy respectively. However, their league woes continued with a 2-1 defeat away at fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic last Saturday.

As for Sheffield Wednesday, they claimed a valuable three points in Dave Challinor’s first League One game last weekend. Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di’Shon Bernard scored on the way to an important 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle, marking the Owls’ first league victory in four matches.

SWFC have to get back on track on the road though, having lost back-to-back games against Notts County and Doncaster Rovers by 2-0 scorelines as Henrik Pedersen‘s tenure came to an end. Wednesday now sit 5th, six points away from the automatic promotion spots.

“Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday are in drastically contrasting positions. The Tykes are lingering in the League One relegation zone with continued discontent towards the ownership, while SWFC are hoping to challenge for promotion as they rebuild under ambitious leadership.

“Daniel Stendel marked an exciting summer appointment at Oakwell but he has been completely hung out to dry. The decline in quality of that squad is just saddening, and with 24 goals conceded this season, I have little faith that their defence can curtail the visitors’ quality this Friday.

“SWFC are finding their feet under Dave Challinor, but the 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle marked an exciting result in his first league game. Davis Keillor-Dunn is in fine form and Di’Shon Bernard is a true Championship quality centre-back, and a big asset at this level.

“Perhaps the occasion can motivate Stendel’s young side and drive them to a surprise result. However, you can’t help but feel the visitors win in pretty comfortable fashion at Oakwell.”

“Barnsley are in serious danger of being relegated this season. Their form has been abysmal at home and with no clean sheets at Oakwell this term, they will be up against it on Friday.

“It’s a great opportunity for the Tykes to incite revenge on the Owls who beat them in the play-off final three years ago. However, the difference in squad talent is a lot greater this time around.

“Sheffield Wednesday have been terrific on the road and with an average of 1.67 points a game, promotion is a real possibility. However, two losses away from home in a row should give a glimmer of hope to Stendel’s side.

“I can’t see the hosts winning this one, though, and Challinor will be eager to continue his winning start as boss. I think SWFC will be far too strong on the night.”

#2131. Athletic: Fernandes still an option for Milan after second contract rejection – the situation

It seems Bruno Fernandes could still be an option for AC Milan, with the star rejecting two contract offers from Manchester United.

In the summer, Milan were rumoured to be interested in a move for Fernandes, who’d always seemed to be a fan of Ruben Amorim. So, with the continuous links to Portuguese players, the Manchester United captain being linked made even more sense.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, no move was made, with him not being seen as a priority, but that may change.

According to The Athletic, via MilanPosts on X, the Portuguese star could still be an option for the Rossoneri in the upcoming mercato(s). Earlier this week, it was reported – again by The Athletic – that he’d rejected a second offer from the Red Devils, so his future is more than up in the air.

The €65 million release clause will not be able to be used, as it expired in the summer. So, the Diavolo may have to be clever with how they negotiate for a player on the wrong side of 30. With his deal up in the summer, though, things get more interesting, even if Manchester United have the option of a year’s extension.

Mauricio Pochettino – who will arrive after the international break – could change his position, and Fernandes is believed to be waiting for an impact to be made with the new coach. If they don’t click, though, Milan could be waiting on the other side.

When he was Sacked we were 3 points off 4th and awaiting the return of the AFCON players. That is progress, ignore the idiot pot noodle fans that think “just add manager” is enough. They’re the ones that thought Carrick was the Manager we needed.

#2130. De Laurentiis: “Film sul Centenario? De Giovanni ha scritto la sceneggiatura, Amazon lo porterà nel mondo

Aurelio De Laurentiis, presidente del Napoli, è stato tra i protagonisti della prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, manifestazione dedicata alle personalità che si sono distinte nel panorama calcistico nazionale. L’evento si è svolto a Villa Campolieto, a Ercolano, dove il patron azzurro ha ricevuto un riconoscimento nella categoria Fair Play, che vedeva tra i finalisti anche Andrea Belotti e Luca Percassi. Nel corso del suo intervento, De Laurentiis ha parlato anche del film dedicato al Centenario del Napoli: “La sceneggiatura del film del centenario la scrive il qui presente Maurizio de Giovanni. Il calcio in Inghilterra è nato con gli aristocratici. Non era un fatto popolare. Arrivarono a Napoli e iniziarono a giocare con gli scugnizzi. Il 1922 sembrerebbe la vera data, poi procrastinata al 1926 per la nascita del Napoli. Che non si chiama Società Sportiva, ma Calcio Napoli. Questo film è venuto talmente bene che una piattaforma importante come Amazon lo porterà nel mondo. Quando abbiamo vinto lo Scudetto con Conte, ho fatto un film e sono andato a Los Angeles: presi questo cinema e ho fatto questa anteprima dove sono arrivati questi tifosi dall’America. C’erano donne emozionatissime che dicevano di non capire nulla di calcio ma che si sono comunque fatte trascinare. Ho scoperto che a San Pedro ci sono 30mila tifosi del Napoli legati all’isola d’Ischia”.

#2128. Lazio-Lecce, Leite può ritrovare Doekhi: Provstgaard verso il riposo

Sutalo rischia almeno due mesi di stop; per Tavares, Gattuso prepara Pedraza sulla corsia sinistra.

Diogo Leite è destinato a sostituire l'infortunato Sutalo nella difesa della Lazio già contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, Gennaro Gattuso deve modificare l'assetto anche per lo stop di Tavares: sulla sinistra il posto dell'ex Arsenal sarà preso da Pedraza.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Al centro della difesa potevano esserci dubbi, ma le indicazioni arrivate dal campo portano a Leite. Sutalo rischia di restare fuori per almeno due mesi. A Formello si spera che la lesione muscolare del croato, ex Ajax, sia meno grave del previsto, anche se i segnali degli ultimi giorni non sono positivi.

L'assenza del difensore pesa sulle scelte per il Lecce. Gattuso ha però mostrato piena fiducia nel portoghese e si prepara ad affidargli il posto di Sutalo.

Per Leite sarebbe un'occasione per trovare più spazio dopo un avvio di stagione dal minutaggio limitato. Il difensore è arrivato a inizio settembre a parametro zero, subito dopo la chiusura del mercato. Ha raccolto sei presenze ed è rimasto in panchina soltanto contro Venezia e Juventus.

#2126. Watford’s midfield struggles will continue until reinforcements are signed – here’s three January targets they must consider

A major issue for Watford this campaign has been the midfield. The summer departure of Imran Louza was a major blow, with his technical qualities, set-piece delivery and ability to dictate games sorely missed.

Similarly, Giorgi Chakvetadze’s transfer to Udinese has left the Hornets devoid of a creative spark, with his tendency to drift centrally and unlock defences. The club have simply not recruited adequate replacements, and they are suffering for it.

The current midfield options at Vicarage Road consist of Hector Kyprianou, Edo Kayembe, Edoardo Bove, and recent signing Martin Payero. None of these options are particularly offensive or astute going forward, lacking the ball-carrying and forward-thinking impetus of Chakvetadze, and the game-changing potential of Louza.

In order for Watford to change their fortunes this season, the club’s hierarchy need to address the glaring issues in midfield. Here, we put forward three targets the Hornets should consider moving for ahead of the January transfer window.

Patrick Kelly had a breakout season for Barnsley in 2025/26, establishing himself as one of League One’s most exciting prospects. He was touted for a potential step up, but stayed put and has remained a standout at Oakwell.

A busy and energetic player, Kelly could well offer Watford the spark they need in midfield. His excellent dribbling and physical attributes would complement a side in need of inspiration and dynamism. He ranks among the top 10% of players in his position League One for dribbles completed (FotMob).

Barnsley have had a disastrous start to the current campaign, and as such, a cut-price deal for the 22 year old could tempt clubs further up the footballing ladder.

Bate has been a critical part of highflying Stockport County’s success this season. The diminutive playmaker has contributed four assists and started all but one of the Hatters’ league games this campaign. He excels with his technical ability, ball retention and progression, and eye for a pass.

Having put behind him his injury issues from last season, he appears to have recaptured his impressive form from the 2024/45 campaign, cementing himself as a potential coup for alert Championship sides.

At 24 years of age, he represents a good blend of experience and potential to improve further. His position as club captain further demonstrates the leadership qualities necessary to navigate a Championship relegation scrap, which may await at Watford.

Hull City’s promotion and busy summer window has left players such as Kieran Dowell with limited minutes, opening the door to a potential exit. Dowell has been omitted from the Tigers’ Premier League squad, and the prospect of a January exit appears increasingly likely.

Dowell has donned the colours of six different Championship clubs, and has developed a reputation for scoring spectacular goals, as well as being an apt creator and technician. With three promotions at this level, he has the necessary pedigree and experience.

Out of contract in the summer, Dowell would represent a cost-effective option on either a short-term deal or a loan. His lack of playing time in recent seasons is a potential concern, but should he regain match fitness quickly he could be a useful addition to a threadbare Watford midfield.

As Watford seek to steer clear of the Championship’s lower reaches, bolstering the midfield is of high importance. The only summer addition in this area, Martin Payero, has been underwhelming when given the opportunity.

The fitness issues plaguing Edoardo Bove, the most talented player of the current options, has further stunted Watford’s progress.

The January window offers the club a chance to make amends for poor summer transfer business and to provide the squad with the best opportunity to consolidate their Championship status. The three midfield options put forward would help to push the club in the right direction.

#2123. 3 strikers West Ham should target in January as Scott Parker sets new talisman demand

West Ham have the busy December schedule to see to before the January transfer window comes around, but Scott Parker is already intent on improving his squad. And, he’s identified two areas where he wants to sign new players: striker and left-back.

The centre-forward has been a position of contention for WHUFC, despite the fact they are the league’s top scorers with a remarkable 37 goals in 15 games. None of Joel Piroe, Pablo or Taty Castellanos have proven they can find consistent goalscoring form, and the latter reportedly wants to leave the London Stadium.

With that in mind, we put forward three strikers West Ham should target to resolve their dilemma.

Parker is said to prefer Championship experience, so who better than someone who is already starring in the division? Andri Gudjohnsen has been in scintillating form for Blackburn Rovers, with a goals per shot rate of 0.50 ranking him among the most clinical finishers in Europe this season.

The 24-year-old has scored 11 goals in 15 games this term and has starred on the international stage for Iceland too. Gudjohnsen scored four in two games over the November break.

A fast and powerful forward with smart movement and finishing, Gudjohnsen could come in and lead the line for West Ham and he’d be backed to make the step up to the Premier League too. It would not be a cheap signing, but he could be just what Parker needs.

Looking slightly further afield, one man who could catch the Hammers’ eye is Paulos Abraham. The 24-year-old was highly rated in his youth but a spell at Dutch side FC Groningen didn’t go as hoped, resulting in his return to Sweden with Hammarby IF.

Since returning to the Allsvenskan in January 2025, he has been one of the league’s most dangerous forwards. 17 goals in 28 league games this season take Abraham to 34 goals in 74 outings for the club, and he was rewarded with his first Sweden call-up earlier this season.

Abraham would bring electric pace to West Ham’s frontline, and his inventive finishing sees him score from unlikely situations. His ability to run beyond Championship defences could bring a new threat to a highly creative WHUFC outfit.

Last but not least is certainly the most ambitious of the lot. However, Aleksandar Mitrovic has had a slightly disrupted recent spell in the Middle East due to a ligament injury and may be tempted to return to London under the lead of Parker again.

The Serbian powerhouse played and starred under the new West Ham boss at Fulham, and he would be a dream addition for Parker. Mitrovic is one of the most prolific forwards in Championship history with 85 goals in 126 games at the level and he would certainly fit the bill as a prolific scorer who can lead the Hammers to promotion.

The main obstacle is obvious though. Mitrovic is on massive money in Qatar with Al-Rayyan, and even if WHUFC can persuade the club to let him leave, the 32-year-old might not be minded to leave his sizeable contract.

But, if the opportunity was there, Mitrovic would be a perfect solution for Parker’s striker issue.

#2120. Leeds United, Nottingham Forest set sights on potential deal for Watford prospect

Watford are on the lookout for new players to bring into their ranks, but they’ve found some fresh prospects in the academy setup too. Amin Nabizada has made a name for himself this term, and among those hoping to follow in his footsteps is Jamael John-Baptiste.

However, the Hornets could have a fight on their hands in the bid to keep the teenage striker. Football Insider reports that Premier League pair Leeds United and Nottingham Forest are both interested in poaching John-Baptiste from the setup at Vicarage Road.

Watford hope to retain John-Baptiste, but his Premier League admirers are watching developments closely ahead of a potential swoop. He signed scholarship terms ahead of the 2025/26 season, and with no professional deal in place, it is believed that his contract runs out at the end of the current campaign.

Watford have given John-Baptiste a chance to prove himself after spells in the Spurs and Brentford academies, and he has delivered for the U18s. That could help them in their bid to keep him, as he may well be eager to pay back those who gave him a chance – much like Sydie Peck at Sheffield United.

However, Leeds United and Nottingham Forest are attractive clubs with strong academy setups. Not only have plenty of prospects come through their ranks and into the first-team squad over the years, but they will be able to offer elite facilities and a higher level of coaching than the Hornets.

If their interest does firm up, it could make keeping John-Baptiste a tough task. For now though, he will remain focused on delivering in the Watford academy to strengthen his reputation and continue his progression.

John-Baptiste is clearly a bright prospect, and one who Watford may well hope breaks into the first-team.

However, it has been a rarity for academy-reared prospects to break through at Vicarage Road. Nabizada has done so this term, but otherwise, the likes of Albert Eames and James Clarridge have only really been called upon to offer depth.

If the Hornets want to have a better chance of retaining talents like John-Baptiste for the foreseeable, they have to forge a clearer route to the first team. If not, then clubs of Leeds United and Nottingham Forest’s ilk will be able to poach youngsters.

Time will tell what comes of John-Baptiste’s situation though, as interest starts to emerge.

#2117. The EFL Championship's top 9 wealthiest owners in 2026/27

The 2026-27 Championship is firmly underway and it's as intriguing as ever.

And with two more play-off spots opening up for the 2026-27 season, the chase for the Premier League riches is more hotly-contested than ever in the second tier of English football.

New financial measures are also coming into place, with profit & sustainability rules (PSR) being taken away and incoming are squad cost rules (SCR), where owners can only invest £33 million in equity over a three-year period, whilst player and manager costs can only amount to 85 per cent of a club's yearly turnover.

Owners tend to need deep pockets to fund a promotion-chasing club in the Championship - but who are the nine wealthiest owners in the second tier ahead of next season? FLW takes a look...

For the longest time, Norwich City were ran by celebrity chef Delia Smith and her husband Michael Wynn-Jones, having joined the club's board in 1996 before becoming majority shareholders in 1998.

Seeking outside investment though for someone with far deeper pockets than themselves, enter Mark Attanasio, who after initially being appointed as a director at Carrow Road in 2022, became the majority shareholder in 2024 - much like how Smith and Wynn-Jones came to being in control 26 years prior.

With prior experience and ownership at Baseball side the Milwaukee Brewers, Attanasio was seen as an ideal fit to take Norwich to the next level, and he now owns 85 per cent of the Norfolk outfit - with a net worth of $1.9 billion (£1.4 billion), according to Forbes, the 68-year-old certainly has the cash to try and take them back to the Premier League.

Blackburn Rovers are into their 16th year of the Venky's ownership, and to say it's been turbulent would be an understatement.

The glory days of Jack Walker's ownership had long gone when the Indian poultry giants purchased the Lancashire outfit from Walker's trust in 2010, but under their guidance, relegation from the Premier League came in 2012 - and they've never returned.

Despite the Rao family not attending a match since January 2013, they still continue to fund the club's annual losses, even if in recent times there has been struggles getting money out of their native India and to the UK, but they have a lot of finance, and as per a report from The News in 2025, the Venky's were worth an estimated £1.56 billion.

With restrictions from the High Court of Delhi now lifted ahead of 2026-27, could the Venky's be ready to invest more into the club's squad to guide them away from another potential relegation battle? Only time will tell...

The Coates family have been involved in Stoke City since 1986, when Peter Coates became majority shareholder and chairman, but after selling to an Icelandic consortium in 1999, he would return seven years later, and in 2015, his son John would become vice-chairman.

Coates junior has worked his way up the ranks since, and in 2024, a change to the ownership structure saw John become sole owner of the club, and he is the one pulling the strings and making the big decisions on who comes and goes at the bet365 Stadium.

Bet365 has been a big business win for the Coates family, and as per Forbes' real-time net worth analysis, Coates himself is worth an estimated £2.3 billion, and despite Stoke's stagnation in the Championship recently, there's seemingly no sign of the funding stopping at the Staffordshire club.

QPR have had turbulent ownership changes over the years, with the eras of Flavio Briatore and Bernie Ecclestone, then Tony Fernandes well and truly in the past.

The current ownership group at Loftus Road is mainly led by Malaysian businessman Ruben Gnanalingam, who owns just under 60 per cent of the Hoops, US investor Richard Reilly holds 21 per cent and former chairman Amit Bhatia also holding 20 per cent.

Whilst Gnanalingam's personal wealth isn't known, the family wealth sits at a healthy £2.3 billion, as per Forbes, with much of their successful business coming from the shipping industry in the form of Westports Holdings.

Gnanalingam is the executive chairman and group managing director of the company, with the 49-year-old being a part of the furniture in the QPR hierarchy since the Fernandes days in 2011 - that doesn't look set to change anytime soon, and with signings recently such as Richard Kone and Ronnie Edwards, he's definitely been putting his money where his mouth is.

From the outside looking in, it may represent something of a surprise that, in Steve Lansdown, Bristol City have the fifth-richest owner at Championship level.

The Bristolian has held his position as chairman of the Robins since 2002, and is the founder of Bristol Sport alongside coupling his duties at Ashton Gate with a majority shareholder role with both Bristol Bears and Bristol Flyers.

This means that, as per Forbes, Lansdown's net worth sits at a whopping £2.38 billion. However, in contrast to other counterparts both on this list and outside of it, the 73-year-old's personal wealth has hardly been translated into a healthy transfer warchest for the Robins to utilise over the years.

Lansdown has undertaken serious work away from the field to help Bristol City grow, such as the impressive £40 million redevelopment of Ashton Gate around a decade ago, although his lack of investment into the playing squad has been a frequent point of frustration for supporters.

The Robins have significant potential and all the foundations are in place for that to be achieved, bar one - you do get the impression that they need to finally make a real splash on signings to get to that next level and threaten to head to the Premier League for the first time in the club's long history.

When you look at how Portsmouth owner Michael Eisner has made his billions, it's no great shock that few second-tier sides can boast a wealthier chief than the New York native - even if, once again, that isn't always reflected in the club's transfer activity.

As per the Los Angeles Business Journal in 2024, Eisner has accumulated a net worth of $3.8 billion (£2.83 billion), having formerly held the role of Disney's CEO for more than 20 years before entering the world of football ownership by taking over Pompey nine years ago.

FLW takes a look at which Championship clubs have the highest wage bill heading into the new season

John Mousinho hasn't been totally without backing in recent years, and Pompey's exile from the Championship has ended under Eisner's ownership, but his investment continues to be patient and methodical without throwing everything towards bringing Premier League football back to Fratton Park - although the summer of 2026 has definitely seen a more 'shackles off' approach at Fratton Park.

We know far less about Charlton Athletic owner Joshua Friedman, who is the majority shareholder of a consortium - Global Football Partners - that completed a takeover to purchase the South London outfit from Thomas Sandgaard in the summer of 2023.

Indeed, official net worth estimates of Friedman are sparse. However, if claims of $5 billion (£3.72 billion) are to be believed, then Charlton very much have a wealthy board, and that has shone through in recent times.

The Addicks' investment has amplified since returning to the Championship through the League One play-offs in May of last year, which preceded - as per Transfermarkt - a summer spending spree under Nathan Jones worth €11.62 million (£10.07 million) as the likes of Rob Apter, Thomas Kaminski, Charlie Kelman and Harvey Knibbs all made their way to the Valley and ultimately helped to keep the side afloat.

There are a number of shareholders on the board at West Ham, and until June, the two largest stakes belonged to controversial chairman David Sullivan and his family, and Daniel Kretinsky, at 38.8% and 27% respectively.

That changed though recently, with Czech businessman Kretinsky and his consortium's stake rising to 43 per cent after a deal was struck with Vanessa Gold - and that could lead to a more ambitious Hammers going into 2026-27.

As per the Sunday Times Rich List of 2025 (via the BBC), Kretinsky's wealth comes in at $10 billion (£8.68 billion), which is a clear second in the Championship when it comes to riches.

Sullivan has ploughed heavy investment into West Ham over the years, much of which was done alongside the late David Gold, although he's hardly a popular figure at the London Stadium owing to the decision to move out of Upton Park and, more recently, a seemingly-endless series of big-money signings who have failed to deliver - and that's ultimately why the East Londoners will be playing Championship football next season for the first time since 2012.

Under Kretinsky's largest stakeholding though, things may be different, and fans will hope that the owner of Czech energy company EPH and also the owner of Royal Mail will actually be a majority owner when Sullivan decides he wants to sell up his share entirely.

Wolves have the richest owners in the Championship overall, with the Old Gold enduring something of a rollercoaster journey throughout the Fosun Group's 10-year reign in charge at Molineux.

Made up of majority stakeholder Guo Guanchang, Fosun Group CEO Wang Qunbin and interim executive chairman Nathan Shi, Fosun's net worth is not publicly known. The Chinese conglomerate is seriously wealthy, though, and according to Companies Market Cap in June 2025, the total net worth sits at a stunning £20.53 billion.

Who is the best Championship owner? Let us know in the comments!

Following a tumultous couple of years in the Premier League, which saw Wolves relegated in dead-last in 25/26, the Molineux faithful will now be hoping that Fosun can show the same level of investment and ambition back in the Championship just as they did when the side last graced the division, going up as champions after signing the likes of Ruben Neves and the late Diogo Jota.

#2116. Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones left unhappy at FA rule change

Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones is one of "a number" of head coaches in the top four leagues in England to have objected to the yellow card rules bestowed upon managers.

It has been the case since the 2018/19 campaign that cautions could be shown to the dugouts in the EFL, with the Premier League following suit the following year. Traditionally, a manager would have to receive four yellow cards before they would receive a touchline ban.

However, in an update to the rules ahead of the 2023/24 term, the FA introduced a 'Participant Behaviour Charter' to maintain a positive environment across the top-flight, the EFL, the Women's Super League and the National League System (Steps 1-4).

The new charter brought in the current rule that a manager only has to be shown three yellow cards to receive a touchline ban, with the cut-off point being the 37th game of the season. Unsurprisingly, Jones, one of the more animated coaches in the game, is against that.

According to Standard Sport, Charlton boss Nathan Jones is among several head coaches who don't like the reduction to how many yellow cards lead to a touchline for a manager.

Managers across the 92 had a meeting recently to discuss the effectiveness of these rules, and Jones, among others, believes that the threshold is incredibly short, especially with managers under much more pressure and scrutiny than ever before, it seems.

Additionally, in comparison to players, who pick up a one-match suspension for five yellow cards by the 19th game of the season, and a two-match ban if they collect 10 by the 37th, a touchline ban for just three cautions by the 37th for a manager seems incredibly harsh.

Head coaches find themselves booked if they are caught out of their technical areas, and they also receive yellow cards if there are any infringements in the dugout that a referee cannot attribute to one person. As the 'most senior' member of staff, they are the ones responsible for controlling things.

Nathan Jones will be one of the few managers who fall victim to these cards, and he is understandably looking for the rules to be relaxed.

Ultimately, certain head coaches will feel that these rules almost limit how well they can do their jobs, especially someone like Jones, who isn't afraid to let his emotions show.

The Welshman was seen almost joining a late attack against Hull City last season, and hung off the dugout after his side scored a late equaliser against Burnley this term, among other crazy things that only someone like Jones is associated with.

Having his actions limited on the sidelines may be detrimental to how much he can motivate his side, especially given how infrequent these sanctions can be.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

Not every departure from a technical area is a yellow card, as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, another very animated manager, rightly pointed out in late October after he admitted he was clipping up infringements from his fellow coaches after he was accused of spending more time out of his little box than others were.

So, managers already feel as if they are walking on eggshells; such is the nature of the job, but sanctions like these can often make it even more of a nervous place.

However, despite Jones and other managers' grumbles, the FA can point to a 17% decrease in technical area cautions since the start of the 2023/24 campaign when the three-yellow-card rule was implemented.

What do you think about the manager yellow card rules? Let us know in the comments.

The numbers indicate that things are working, but again, managers may point to the infrequency of the rules as the reason for that. Not every infringement should be a yellow card, but the reasons why they are being handed out aren't something that coaches agree on.

Time will tell whether the Charlton boss, and others who oppose the rule change, will have their way and see the yellow card threshold increase once more, but with the success of the charter so far, it may be difficult for them to persuade the FA.

#2113. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

#2110. Leeds vs Man Utd preview: Team news, form, injuries and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable with a recurring shin problem, while Patrick Dorgu is expected to be out until late November. Manuel Ugarte is recovering from knee surgery, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt with a back problem.

There is better news regarding Matthijs de Ligt, who could return to contention. Leny Yoro is also available for selection despite his Champions League suspension.

#2109. West Brom officially announce Shilen Patel action and it's triggered a response

West Bromwich Albion's impressive start to the Championship season has now got even better in the eyes of the club's supporters, courtesy of a major off-field development involving owner, Shilen Patel.

The American businessman took control of the Baggies for £60m in February 2024, bringing a welcomed end to Guochuan Lai's controversial tenure in The Hawthorns boardroom.

Not all has been straightforward for the Black Country outfit since then, with activity linked to former ownership groups proving to be a strong stumbling block in Patel's aims of moving the club forward.

Albion narrowly avoided a first relegation to League One in 33 years last season through a strong end-of-season run under James Morrison, who has since vindicated Patel's decision to make his managerial role permanent with his side sat fifth after 15 games played, just one point off the Championship summit.

Supporters are now believing a bright future for their club is ensured after confirmation that Patel has paid off an outstanding £3.7m loan was confirmed on Wednesday afternoon.

West Brom were hit with a two-point deduction in May for breaching the EFL's PSR regulations, which left many supporters perplexed given the high-profile sales of Torbjørn Heggem and Tom Fellows in 2025.

12 months previous, it was confirmed Patel would pay off the aforementioned loan, which was taken out by West Bromwich Football Holdings in 2014 by former owner Jeremy Peace, after an investigation saw the liability of the funds passed to his company, Bilkul Football WBA.

"At that time, the club confirmed arrangements had been put in place to ensure it would not sustain any loss in respect of the loan," a statement on Albion's website read.

"The club can confirm the outstanding liability, including interest, has now been repaid in full by the current ownership group."

This isn't the first loan Patel has paid off during his tenure, having wiped out an outstanding sum to Wisdom Smart Corporation Limited in March 2024, although a further loan to MSD Holdings is still outstanding.

Nevertheless, supporters in B71 have been quick to hail the 46-year-old's work, with one saying: "Saved the club when it was at its lowest point. Top people who deserve all the respect possible from fans. Here's to the future."

Another Baggies fan wrote: "We should forever be grateful to Shilen Patel and the ownership group. I don't know where they will eventually take us, but whatever happens in the future they deserve our patience and support."

"Words won't ever express what Shilen has done for us, from the worst excuse for an owner to someone like him who cares and loves the club and has saved us along the way, forever grateful," further summed up the feeling Albion's fanbase have towards the Florida-born entrepreneur.

"Another huge weight lifted off the shoulders of the club. Grateful to Bilkul and Shilen," was another comment full of praise.

Baggies fans, what is your initial reaction to this news? Comment below!

Summing up the loan payment in a rather humourous way, one Albion fan added: "BILKUL AND PATELLLLL 90+12 years."

Another posted: "This is brilliant from Shilen. But the next statement in Dec saying the MSD loan is fully paid off is gonna be unreal!! Cannot thank Shilen for saving our club and giving us a direction!"

With West Brom returning to action this weekend following the international break, their supporters will certainly be in a jubilant mood as they prepare to take on Swansea City in South Wales, with their hosts seemingly in disarray as Vitor Matos nears his expected move to RC Strasbourg.

Albion's future is certainly in safe hands right now, though, with Patel finally able to repay the aforementioned loan, whilst the transfer strategy adopted in the summer means there are several names within Morrison's ranks capable of delivering in the here and now before potentially being sold on for millions.

The Baggies have certainly had a mixed time under Patel's stewardship, but which players have been the best value for money?

Whilst supporters will certainly be getting carried away with such news given West Brom's previous turmoil, Morrison and his players will be fully focused on the task in hand, which, at present, will be to ensure they remain in the promotion picture given how congested the Championship table currently is.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

#2104. Sheffield Wednesday & Dave Challinor sent automatic promotion warning

EFL pundits Callum Fowler and Tom Garratt have questioned whether Sheffield Wednesday can win automatic promotion from League One this season ahead of a tough run of upcoming fixtures.

As a new era begins at the club following David Storch's takeover, it has been a turbulent start to life back in League One for Wednesday, with inconsistent results forcing the club into an early season managerial change.

Wednesday parted company with manager Henrik Pedersen last month after a run of just one win from six games, and they did not take long to appoint his replacement, former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor.

The Owls were knocked out of the FA Cup in Challinor's first game in charge as they were beaten 2-1 by League Two side Oldham Athletic before a much-changed side were thrashed 4-0 by Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy, but the 51-year-old secured his first victory at the first attempt with a 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle at Hillsborough on Saturday.

It was not the most convincing of performances from Wednesday, but they produced a clinical display against one of their promotion rivals, with goals from Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard getting Challinor's reign up and running.

Ahead of the trip to face South Yorkshire rivals at Oakwell on Friday night, the Owls currently sit fifth in the League One table, and they are just six points behind second-placed Stockport County and leaders Huddersfield Town.

On the latest edition of The Pyramid podcast, Fowler and Garratt discussed Wednesday's automatic promotion hopes, and the pair claimed that it will be easier to assess their top two chances after their challenging upcoming run of fixtures.

When asked if the victory over Plymouth marked the start of a title push for the Owls, Fowler said: "No, but they're definitely finishing top six.

"I want to see what they're like on Friday against us (Barnsley).

"A game like that definitely has potential for them to slip up."

However, Garratt disagreed that the clash at Oakwell would be a test for Challinor's men, responding: "That's a tap-in for them.

"They've got Stevenage away on the Tuesday, that's a tough game, then Reading at home, then Oxford, then Leicester, then Luton.

"After the tap-in on Friday, they've actually got a run where you can start judging them.

"Barnsley away at the minute is like playing a secondary school team."

"I still think Sheffield Wednesday have definitely got a good chance of top two," Garratt added.

Fowler was less confident about Wednesday's automatic promotion prospects, replying: "I think Huddersfield and Stockport will definitely finish in front of them, so that wipes it out for me.

"I think Wednesday will at least finish where they are now."

Can Sheffield Wednesday win automatic promotion from League One under Dave Challinor this season? Tell us in the comments below!

With a tough fixture schedule and mounting injury list, it could be a tricky first few weeks in charge at Hillsborough for Challinor, but Saturday's victory over Plymouth has certainly got Wednesday supporters excited about what could be ahead under their new manager.

It is difficult to disagree with Fowler that Huddersfield and Stockport are the standout teams in the division at present, while Oxford United have made an impressive start to life under Aaron Ramsey, but there is still plenty of time for the Owls to force their way into the automatic promotion mix.

Given that Challinor led Stockport to two consecutive play-off finishes in League One before his departure from Edgeley Park this summer, Wednesday fans will be confident of at least securing a top six spot, and they may be hoping for even better than that.

#2103. Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

#2102. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

#2101. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2100. Arsenal face January dilemma as Liverpool and Chelsea join Alex Scott transfer race

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott. Mikel Arteta may have to rethink his transfer plans if competition for the midfielder intensifies.

According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old. The clubs want to establish what it would take to persuade Bournemouth to sell. However, none appears close to agreeing to a deal.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move. Liverpool and Chelsea are more interested in signing Scott in January. However, if they were to make a serious offer, it could be hard to hold out.

Scott has become one of the most exciting midfielders in the Premier League. He is an attractive option for clubs looking to improve their squad going forward due to his age, experience and being a homegrown player.

However, there is some uncertainty around Scott’s future. The England international has turned down two contract offers and is unwilling to sign a new deal. There are 18 months left on Scott’s contract, meaning it is an increasingly important decision for Bournemouth.

Arsenal are interested in Scott with doubts surrounding their own midfield options. There have been reports linking Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino to exits.

Scott would give Arteta another option, but Arsenal will have to consider if they want to make a move and give Liverpool and Chelsea an advantage.

Bournemouth are reported to want more than £100m to let him go during the January transfer window.

It would be a big asking price, especially given that Scott has 18 months left on his contract. There are a few reasons why Bournemouth could be holding out for a big fee.

The Cherries had to pay £25m to bring Scott in from Bristol City, who will receive 20 per cent of any future transfer fee. They will also have to find a suitable replacement at the halfway stage.

Reports said Chelsea received a number of offers worth around £70m in the summer, but Bournemouth have rejected claims that a bid of £80m will get them talking.

Scott is believed to be happy to stay at the club until the end of the campaign. Bournemouth are also having a great season under Marco Rose, currently sitting in seventh place in the Premier League with eight straight wins in all competitions.

Arsenal have little to hurry into any deal and could use the summer to negotiate a better deal. This is especially true with Scott’s contract situation becoming more of an issue.

The problem is that Liverpool and Chelsea are keen competitors and could lead to a bidding war in January, leaving Arsenal with little room to negotiate.

Whilst Arsenal have made their interest known, this doesn’t necessarily mean he will be moving anytime soon. If Scott is a genuine target, then they must be prepared to pounce if the situation arises.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand said.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

#2098. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.

The striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season. His latest comments suggest he will not be seeking a move away from north London.

Gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer. He’s played a key role in the club winning the Premier League last season with 14 league goals.

However, he has not featured as much this season. Kai Havertz often being Arteta’s go-to man centrally, resulting in him only starting once in the Premier League.

This has led to some speculation that the Sweden international may look at his options in January. However, his latest interview with the Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen suggests otherwise.

Gyökeres was asked if he wants to stay at Arsenal and has made it clear he wants to continue his career at the Emirates.

The striker also spoke about his relationship with Arteta.

He explained that they regularly discuss football, the team’s approach and the opposition. Those conversations also help him understand what Arteta expects when he is selected to start.

It is a key point to note that just because he hasn’t had much time on the pitch doesn’t mean there have been any issues between the two.

Gyökeres has begun to show his worth again in recent weeks. He found the net against Fleetwood in the League Cup and then Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

This came after a long time to get his first goal of the season and gives him the chance to remind Arteta what he can bring to the team.

There is no doubt that Gyökeres has not lived up to the expectations he had when he came from Portugal.

But his overall effect cannot be ignored. He has contributed 23 goals and 6 assists in 69 games for Arsenal.

The challenge will be finding a way to get the best out of him and Havertz. They add different attributes, and Arteta will have plenty of options to choose from depending on the opposition.

They will also want to avoid losing someone they have invested heavily in so early on. Gyökeres has a contract until 2030, so they are in a great position.

His latest comments will help to reassure fans that he is not looking to leave the club after stating his ambition to play more games and make himself an indispensable part of Arteta’s squad.

The main thing for Arsenal will be to make sure that he can turn this attitude into consistent performances. Gyökeres has made his intentions clear and now needs to show why they brought him to North London in the first place.

#2096. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2095. Sheffield Wednesday star Barry Bannan posts hilarious Aston Villa throwback

Sheffield Wednesday icon Barry Bannan is closing in on 500 appearances for the Owls, having returned to the club in the summer. However, he's not always been at Hillsborough and was actually quite the journeyman at the start of his career.

It was at Aston Villa where it all started for the Scottish international, having taken on an opportunity with the club after a couple of years with Celtic's youth academy.

Bannan's debut came in December 2008 in a UEFA Cup clash with Hamburg - a game that saw Villa lose 3-1. That was around the time that the 36-year-old had signed his first professional contract with the club, a moment that he's been reflecting on.

Over on Instagram, Bannan is particularly active on his story, sharing photos and comments.

On Wednesday morning, he shared an image of the day he signed his first professional contract with Villa, around 2008, surrounded by what looks like family, a potential agent and/or club officials.

Bannan can quite clearly see the funny side of the image that was taken 18 years ago, with a laughing emoji accompanying the words: "First ever pro contract at Aston Villa flashback".

The midfielder would play 82 times for Villa in all competitions, scoring two goals. In the period that he was at Villa Park, he had loans with Derby County, Blackpool and Leeds United, before sealing a move to Crystal Palace on summer transfer deadline day 2013.

Bannan was a tidy footballer at Villa and highly-rated young midfielder. His time at Palace brought a loan to Bolton and, ultimately, wasn't the success that the South London club had hoped.

By the time August 2015 came, Bannan was signing with Sheffield Wednesday and tweeting: "Glad to have joined @swfc on a permanent transfer today new start and glad to be going somewhere to play regular football and a fresh start."

Barry Bannan stats at Sheffield Wednesday (18/11/2026)

He got that regular football as Sheffield Wednesday challenged for promotion to the Premier League in his first two years at the club. The Scotland international became a real cult hero in that time, and has subsequently stuck by Wednesday through a lot of on-field and off-field turmoil.

Bannan is now approaching 500 games for the Owls, taking only a short break from representing the club at the start of 2026 when he joined promotion-chasing Millwall at a time Wednesday's off-field turmoil at the hands of Dejphon Chansiri was at its worst.

After returning in the summer, Bannan is eyeing another League One promotion with Sheffield Wednesday - the club that's been his first proper home since he agreed those professional terms with Villa 18 years ago.
